subject: Reserved GPU queueing / p99 latency — clarification & request for variance
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumbank.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Ashlee Kim <ashlee.kim@skyforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed p99 spikes on reserved pool — need guidance

Hi Priya,

We've been seeing intermittent p99 latency spikes (token generation) against our reserved GPU pool over the last 10 days. The app hit short windows where the p99 jumps to ~1.8s from our steady ~0.9s baseline. This is causing small but visible UI jitter for traders during market open.

Attached a heatmap (queueing_p99_heatmap.png) that correlates the spikes with a burst of background batch jobs we run at 08:45 UTC. We're on the reserved 8-GPU pool (commit tier: reserved-8-high) and expected reserved capacity to avoid this.

Can Redwood confirm whether the reserved pool guarantees are intended to prevent these bursts from impacting tail latency? If not, what is the process to request a temporary variance or carveout (we have a finance review this Friday)? Also include next steps if we need to request burst credits or an SLA amendment.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
Helium Bank

[attachment: queueing_p99_heatmap.png (image/png)]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p99 spikes on reserved pool — need guidance

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the data and the heatmap, that's very helpful. Short answer: reserved pools guarantee capacity for throughput (concurrency and sustained tokens/sec) but there are operational edge cases (priority queuing and transient KV-cache warmups) that can produce tail spikes.

I'm looping in Marcus (SRE) to give the technical breakdown and propose mitigations. Laura, adding you for commercial/contract implications — Helium's finance review is Friday so if there's any short-term credit or carving approach we can offer, please advise.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus to confirm root cause and whether throttling/priority preemption happened.
- If queueing preemption occurred, we can propose a one-week burst allowance or temporary priority carveout while Helium staggers background jobs.
- Meanwhile we can fast-track a draft SLA amendment for your legal/finance review (I can share a template).

I'll also attach a draft amendment I can start filling out.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

[attachment: draft_sla_amendment_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p99 spikes on reserved pool — need guidance

Hi all,

Quick technical notes after looking at the heatmap and our logs from the reserved-8-high pool:

- Evidence of short windows (~20-45s) where background batch traffic launched large prefix-heavy requests that caused KV-cache misses across some nodes. Misses triggered longer token latency while the cache warmed.
- We also saw transient preemption of low-priority requests during that window when the pool experienced >95% instantaneous utilization. Our priority scheduler will preempt or enqueue best-effort classes to preserve capacity for guaranteed slots — this affects p99 for best-effort traffic.

Options to mitigate:
1) Operational change on Helium side: shift heavy batch jobs outside market open windows, or introduce a stagger by 2–5 minutes to reduce concurrence. (Low lift)
2) Priority carveout: we can add a temporary carveout that reserves N slots specifically for your latency-sensitive route during peak windows (requires config + short notice for scheduling). (Medium lift, quick)
3) Burst credit: provide a limited burst credit to your account to elevate best-effort traffic priority for a specified window. (Operational + billing approval)
4) SLA amendment: change the definition of p99 for reserved pools to include an explicit carveout or add an availability credit for tail violations. This requires legal & finance and takes ~7–14 business days.

I recommend (2) as the quickest path: we can reserve 2 low-latency slots for your route between 13:45–14:15 UTC for the next 7 days while you rework batch timing. If that sounds OK I'll provision and update routing rules.

Technical ask for you, Sanjay: can you confirm the time window of your batch job in UTC and whether you can shift the start by 5–15 minutes? Also, please share any route names or API keys used so we can target the carveout.

—Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Ashlee Kim <ashlee.kim@skyforge.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p99 spikes on reserved pool — need guidance

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the diagnosis.

Batch window: 08:45–09:05 UTC (daily). We can shift by up to 10 minutes tomorrow if that will help. Route name is /v1/generate/trading-model (key ending -hb-trade).

Please go ahead with the temporary carveout you suggested (2 slots, 13:45–14:15 UTC) for the next 7 days while we test shifting the batch start time. Also Laura — if the carveout triggers any billing or credit discussions, please advise; we want to avoid a procurement loop this week.

Sanjay
Head of Platform, Helium Bank

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@heliumbank.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p99 spikes on reserved pool — clarification & request for variance

All — confirming commercial stance: we can provision the 2-slot priority carveout for Helium Bank for 7 days at no charge to assist with the production risk window, provided we document the timebox and success criteria. If after 7 days there's still impact, we'll escalate to a short-term invoice credit or fast-tracked SLA amendment (per legal).

Action items:
- Marcus: provision carveout starting tomorrow, notify Helium when done.
- Priya: edit the attached draft_sla_amendment_v1.pdf to reflect the timebox and success criteria (p99 <1.1s during carveout windows) and send to Sanjay + finance.
- Stephanie: hold a placeholder for legal review if we need the formal amendment after the trial.

I'll also put a one-page commercial note into the HubSpot deal and flag finance to standby should a credit be needed.

Thanks — Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
